confirmed.title: A name found or typed for the clicked line is also written on every other line whose street is unknown, so street lines the measuring flagged as 'one street or two?' (unsure, needs review) become 'one' and lot width is measured along both streets
confirmed.detail: On a non-corner pick, street_lines_after_pick keeps every line unless the set is already a known 'two'. ids_after_pick then fills every line with no known street with `name`, even though the architect named only the line they clicked. Street lines a=[[0,0],[40,0]] and b=[[40,0],[40,100]] turn 90 degrees, so street_verdict says ('unsure', 90.0) and measure.Lot stops with one_street_or_two (needs review). The architect clicks a and either types 'A St' (when ids are None or [None, None]), or types nothing at all (ids ['A St', None]: street_name_after_pick returns 'A St' and nothing is asked). The result is street_ids ['A St','A St'], so street_verdict says ('one', None). measure.Lot then runs no street check, and lot width is frontage along both streets: 140 ft instead of 40 ft. This is the round-5 P0 (a 40 ft lot read 200 ft wide) coming back through a name pick. It is the same pattern as last round's P1: a name given for one line lands on other lines and two streets become one. The fix only stopped overwriting lines with a known name. The new test even asserts this as intended: `assert logic.ids_after_pick([a, b], None, [a, b], "A St") == ["A St", "A St"]  # nothing known: as typed` (its a and b happen to be collinear). How it can happen: multi-line non-corner street sets with missing or partial names come from hand-edited GordiumFacts, older saved facts (eb627d4 had no street_ids at all), or the round-10 test's own [A St, None, B Ave] shape.
confirmed.evidence:
rhino_logic.ids_after_pick:

street_lines_after_pick keeps every line unless the verdict is 'two':
    if street_verdict(lines, ids)[0] == "two" and ids[hits[0]]: ...
    return [list(map(list, line)) for line in lines]
measure.py: `elif verdict == "unsure": self.street_problem = stop("one_street_or_two", ...)`. 'one' gets no stop.
Reproduced: ids None/[None,None] with 'A St' typed, or ['A St', None] with nothing typed -> {'street_ids': ['A St','A St']}, verdict ('one', None); before the pick it was ('unsure', 90.0).
confirmed.pin: New test in packages/design_checker/tests/test_check.py. With a=[[0,0],[40,0]] and b=[[40,0],[40,100]], for ids in (None, [None, None], ['A St', None]), pick a with the name street_name_after_pick returns (or 'A St' typed). Assert street_verdict(facts['street_line'], facts.get('street_ids'))[0] != 'one'; it should stay 'unsure'. Also change the existing assert `ids_after_pick([a, b], None, [a, b], "A St") == ["A St", "A St"]` to expect the name on the clicked line only.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Put `name` only on the clicked line, and pass `picked` into ids_after_pick. Every other line keeps its known name or stays None, so street_verdict falls back to the drawing (heading check) for lines nobody named. Never spread a name to a line the architect did not name. For a set the lookup named as one street (the sample's eight Ithaca Rd lines), every line is already known, so nothing changes there.
skeptics:
I ran the exact path the plugin uses and the finding holds. In the non-corner branch of gordium_rhino.py:1350-1368, street_name_after_pick runs first. Its result, or the name the architect types, then goes to ids_after_pick together with the lines that street_lines_after_pick returns.

- **street_lines_after_pick (rhino_logic.py:809-829):** it narrows the lines only when the verdict is "two". Otherwise it returns every line.
- **ids_after_pick (rhino_logic.py:781-801):** if matching_ids gives None, it returns [name]*len(lines). If not, every line whose street is unknown gets `name`.
- **street_verdict (street_lines.py:67-79):** returns "one" when every line carries the same name, and never checks the turn in that case.

I ran it with a=[[0,0],[40,0]], b=[[40,0],[40,100]] and the architect clicking a, for three starting states of street_ids:

- None, with 'A St' typed: result ['A St','A St'].
- [None,None], with 'A St' typed: result ['A St','A St'].
- ['A St',None], with nothing typed (street_name_after_pick returns 'A St' on its own): result ['A St','A St'].

In all three cases the verdict went from ('unsure', 90.0) to ('one', None).

measure.py:129-135 stops with one_street_or_two only when the verdict is "unsure", so after the pick the needs-review stop is gone. The non-corner path is reachable whenever corner_lot is not True. This code is new on the branch: eb627d4 had no street_ids and no ids_after_pick. I did not re-run the 140 ft width figure myself. Even so, a 90-degree turn that was "unsure" becoming "one" because of a name given for a single line is the false-pass pattern the finding describes.

I could not refute it, and I reproduced it in the review_arch worktree.

1. ids_after_pick (rhino_logic.py:781-801) gives every line with no known street the name `name`. When no old names match the lines (`old is None`), it writes `[name] * len(lines)`. Otherwise it writes `known(line) or name` for each line.
2. street_lines_after_pick (rhino_logic.py:804-822) narrows the lines only when street_verdict says 'two' and the clicked line has a name. In every other case it returns all the lines.
3. The caller at gordium_rhino.py:1347-1366 (the non-corner 'street' branch) passes the whole line set and the name to ids_after_pick. If street_name_after_pick already found a name, the architect is not asked.
4. In street_lines.py, street_verdict returns 'one' once every line carries the same name, and it skips the turn check. measure.py:129-135 stops with one_street_or_two only on 'unsure'. A 'one' verdict gets no stop.

Repro with a=[[0,0],[40,0]] and b=[[40,0],[40,100]]:
- Before the pick, all three cases (ids None, [None, None], ['A St', None]) give ('unsure', 90.0).
- In all three, the pick ends with street_ids ['A St', 'A St'] and verdict ('one', None).

So a corner that should go to needs review is measured as one street along both lines, which is a false pass. Nothing upstream stops this. matching_ids only checks that there is one name per line. The flow is reachable whenever the facts have several street lines and some names are missing.

confirmed.title: Naming the unknown line on a two-street set keeps the other street's lines, so the pick never settles the front: the check stops on 'two streets' and the box shows only the typed street's name
confirmed.detail: The plugin computes `lines` with the OLD names (b unknown, so every line is kept) and only then merges in the typed name. Corner a(A St), b(None), c(B Ave): the architect clicks b and types 'B Ave'. Saved: street_line [a,b,c], street_ids ['A St','B Ave','B Ave'], verdict 'two'. A non-corner lot then stops with two_streets (needs review, so not a false pass). But the architect just picked B Ave as the front and has to click b a second time before the set narrows to [b,c]. Meanwhile saved_ui['street_name']='B Ave' makes the Front lot line row read 'B Ave' while the blue highlight still covers A St's line.
confirmed.evidence:
lines = logic.street_lines_after_pick(facts.get("street_line"), picked, ids=facts.get("street_ids"))   # old ids: b unknown -> all lines
logic.set_street_lines(facts, lines, logic.ids_after_pick(..., lines, name))
saved_ui["street_name"] = name
Reproduced: first pick -> ['A St','B Ave','B Ave'], ('two', None); a second identical pick -> [[b],[c]].
confirmed.pin: Test: with [a,b,c] and ids ['A St', None, 'B Ave'], pick b and type 'B Ave' through the plugin's own sequence (a single rhino_logic helper the plugin calls). Assert the resulting street_line == [b, c] and street_ids == ['B Ave','B Ave'] after ONE pick.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the clicked line its name first (the old ids with `name` put at the clicked index), then call street_lines_after_pick with those updated ids, and save the ids for the lines kept. Put this in one rhino_logic helper the plugin calls, so CI tests the real order of steps rather than a source-string assert.
skeptics:
The finding holds. This code is new on this branch: the diff adds the single-street pick branch at apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:1348-1368. At line 1363 the plugin computes `lines = logic.street_lines_after_pick(facts.get("street_line"), picked, ids=facts.get("street_ids"))` using the old names, before the typed `name` is merged in by `ids_after_pick` at line 1365. At line 1367 it then sets `saved_ui["street_name"] = name`.

In packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:804-825, `street_lines_after_pick` narrows the set to one street only when `ids[hits[0]]` is truthy (line 822). Otherwise it returns every line (line 825). So when the clicked line had no name, every line is kept, including the other street's line.

I ran the scenario with lines a, b, c and names ['A St', None, 'B Ave']. Clicking b and typing 'B Ave' gives lines [a, b, c], names ['A St', 'B Ave', 'B Ave'], and street_verdict ('two', None). Repeating the same click then narrows to [b, c]. That matches the claim exactly.

This is not a false pass: the verdict stays 'two', which stops the check on two streets. It is a real gap between what the architect picked and what is saved. The pick does not settle the front, and the box row shows 'B Ave' while the highlight still includes A St's line. I found no upstream guarantee that prevents this. No other code path does the same thing on purpose, and this case is the one the round-10 docstring of `ids_after_pick` covers ([A St, ?, B Ave] with B Ave typed).

I could not refute this. The finding holds, and the code is new on this branch.

What I read:
- apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:1354-1368 (single-pick street branch). It calls `street_lines_after_pick(facts['street_line'], picked, ids=facts['street_ids'])` using the OLD ids. Only after that does it merge the typed name with `ids_after_pick(...)`, and then it sets `saved_ui['street_name'] = name`.
- packages/design_checker/design_checker/rhino_logic.py:804-822 (`street_lines_after_pick`). It narrows to one street's lines only when `ids[hits[0]]` is truthy. When the clicked line's id is None it returns every line.
- rhino_logic.py:781-801 (`ids_after_pick`). It puts the typed name only on lines whose old id was unknown.

Reproduction: I ran this in packages/design_checker with a=A St, b=None, c=B Ave and line b picked.
- `street_name_after_pick` returns None, so the plugin asks for a name. The architect types 'B Ave'.
- Result: lines [a,b,c], ids ['A St','B Ave','B Ave'], `street_verdict` = ('two', None).
- A second identical pick on the saved facts narrows to [b,c].

So the first pick does not settle the front. The saved name 'B Ave' then shows in the box while the street lines still include A St's line.

Reachability: the branch runs whenever `corner_lot` is not True. Nothing upstream stops two-street ids with one unknown entry from reaching it. `set_street_lines` keeps any ids that match the lines one for one.

The `git diff eb627d4...HEAD` lines 235-237 show this code was added on the branch, so it is not a pre-existing issue.

Severity: this is not a false pass. It ends in "needs review" via two_streets. It is a real correctness/UX defect as described.

priorStatus.title: Clicking a line of unknown street on a two-street set now keeps every line, and the name typed for that one line overwrites the other lines' known street names, so 'two streets' becomes 'one street' and lot width gets measured along both streets
priorStatus.reasoning: ids_after_pick now keeps known names, so the reported [A St, ?, B Ave] case stays 'two' (verified). But the pattern is still there: the name for the clicked line is written on every OTHER line of unknown street, and when old ids are missing on every line. That turns an 'unsure' (needs review) set into 'one', and lot width is measured along both streets. Example: lines turning 90 degrees with ids None, [None,None] or ['A St',None], click a -> ['A St','A St'], verdict 'one'. See the P1 finding.

priorStatus.title: street_lines_after_pick keeps the clicked street's lines by exact string match, but street_verdict compares names after normalising them
priorStatus.reasoning: street_lines_after_pick now filters with street_lines.same_street, which uses the same _norm as street_verdict and is falsy for None. ids[hits[0]] is guaranteed truthy before the filter. The test asserts ['A St','a st.','B Ave'] picking a gives [a, b].
